description: Rust/Python MIT chess library: rules, facts, explanations, PGN, opening books and names, UCI client, and an MCP server over it; one API, Chess960 throughout.
rules: esca is one Rust crate and the Python package built from it: `esca = "0.3"` in Cargo.toml or `pip install esca`. The two surfaces mirror each other name for name; Python names are snake_case.

Position is placement and state only; the rules are a Variant (CLASSIC, CHESS960); Game holds a Variant, a Position and the history, and answers repetition and claims. Castling is stored king-takes-rook; both UCI spellings are read.

Facts answers what is true about a position in fourteen versioned groups (placement, state, material, pawns, pieces, king, mobility, attacks, exchange, threats, tactics, endgame, history, planes), plus 40 values per legal move.

Schema::v1 (esca.SCHEMA) is the versioned contract between the extractor and the net: 2039 f32 per position, 40 per move, identified by schema_id. Encode with esca.encode(fens) / encode_into(fens, out).

explain answers rules questions with evidence, every reason its own field: Position.castling(colour, wing), en_passant_status, pins, skewers, checkers, attackers, between; Game.repetition_status, fifty_move_status, draw_status, claims_after.
Cargo features, off by default: lichess (evaluation-dump reader), pgn, uci (blocking Engine), tokio (async Engine), polyglot (opening books), openings (ECO names).
The Python wheel carries every feature: esca.lichess, esca.pgn, esca.uci (Engine, AsyncEngine, protocol), esca.polyglot, esca.openings. Position.polyglot_key() needs no feature.
cozy-chess is an implementation detail: no cozy_chess type appears in esca's public API. MIT-licensed, and every dependency is permissive.
